meta.hypothesis: Per-primary IRT partitioning loses inter-track reactions (E10f: 96% of the 1us H2 gap). Running the production IRT worker on a GLOBAL radical pool (cross-primary) should recover ~E10f ΔG(H2)=+0.149 at 128 primaries.
meta.method: tools/run_irt_xprimary.cjs: forces pid=0 in a copy of public/irt-worker.js so all radicals share one pool — the existing O(N^2) pairing, heap scheduler, and reaction handling run cross-primary unchanged. Runs per-primary AND cross-primary on the SAME 128-primary subset of the production 10 keV dump (σ_exc=0.5, RECOMB=1.0). Naive O(N^2), tractable at 128 primaries (~7 min); full-N is compute-bound by the dense point-source core (spatial-hash follow-up).
meta.enabled_by: webgpu-dna-native — the global pool needs host RAM, not a browser-tab heap.

status: pass (mechanism validated; E10f framing corrected — coupled tradeoff, not a clean fix)

summary.headline: Cross-primary IRT reproduces E10f: ΔG(H2)=+0.129 @128 primaries (E10f +0.149) — recovers G(H2) 0.458->0.587 (0.74x->0.94x chem6), confirming per-primary partitioning loses inter-track H2 formation. CAVEAT: it also OVER-recombines OH (0.91x->0.70x) and eaq (0.85x->0.54x) at the point-source density — so naive global pooling is not a clean production win; matching chem6 needs the density/geometry resolved (links to the E12-bulk point-source question).

density_sweep.note: cross-primary minus per-primary dG @1us vs K primaries (density in the point-source core)
density_sweep.coupling: dH2 up and dOH/eaq down monotonically together (~3 OH lost per H2 gained) — a coupled tradeoff

summary.decisive_conclusion: No density reproduces chem6 (high H2 AND high OH); the inter-track recombination couples them. E12-bulk (density via spreading) would NOT close the gap. Corrects E10f, which pinned per-primary partitioning as 96% of the 1us gap by looking at H2 ONLY: fixing H2 via cross-primary breaks OH/eaq. chem6 high-H2-and-high-OH must come from a reaction/diffusion difference, not cross-primary pooling. Production keeps per-primary IRT (better OH/eaq).

conclusion: The inter-track mechanism is confirmed and the cross-primary machinery works (enabled by the native runtime). It fixes H2 but over-recombines OH/eaq at our dense point-source core — turning it into a production improvement requires resolving the density/geometry (chem6 geometry vs our point source), and the spatial-hash optimisation for full N.
